title: Understanding Liquidity
hook: Clear Liquidity Detective, pass the Knowledge Check and save your Check-In to unlock Section 2.

game.title: Liquidity Detective 💧
game.tagline: Nine cases. What do we know, and what don’t we know yet?
game.doneLine: You found the sides, the pools and the doors, described sweeps without the story, and kept liquidity where it belongs: context, not an entry rule.

levels.body: Look at the highlighted area. Go fast.

items.why: Below the first low on the chart: sell-side.
Above the first high on the chart: buy-side.

levels.passText: Above highs → buy-side. Below lows → sell-side.
levels.name: Buy-side or sell-side?
levels.goal: Above highs or below lows? Name the side.

debrief.saw: Highlighted areas above highs and below lows.
debrief.know: Above highs: buy-side liquidity. Below lows: sell-side liquidity.
debrief.unknown: Whether price will ever trade into any of them.

steps.text: No labels. Find where orders may gather.

pick.prompt: Tap the most obvious liquidity pool.
pick.hint: Two highs stopped at nearly the same price.

notes.mid: That’s the middle of the move. Nothing obvious sits there.
notes.low2: That low is less obvious than what’s above. Look for a pair.

pick.why: Above the equal highs: an obvious pool area many traders can see.

debrief.saw: Two highs at nearly the same price, and lows below.
debrief.know: Equal highs make an obvious area where buy-side liquidity may rest.
debrief.unknown: How many orders are there, and whether price will reach them.

steps.text: Before you can answer “which liquidity?”, define the room.

pick.hint: The top of the whole range.

notes.el: That’s the bottom of the range.

steps.text: Price just traded above a high inside the range.

options.label: Internal
options.why: Above an internal high, still inside the room.

options.label: External
options.feedback: The external high is far above price.

debrief.saw: An external high far above, and price trading above an internal high.
debrief.know: Price took internal liquidity. The external high is untouched.
debrief.unknown: Whether price will ever reach the external high.

steps.text: One candle closes just above the prior high.

options.label: Acceptance-like
options.feedback: One close isn’t holding and building. Wait.

options.label: Sweep-like
options.feedback: It closed above. You can’t call failure yet.

options.label: Not enough information yet
options.why: Right. One close above is a start, not a whole behavior.

steps.text: Price closes back below and moves away.

options.label: Sweep-like: traded above, failed to sustain

levels.name: Sweep or acceptance?
levels.goal: Let the behavior develop. “Not enough information” is a real answer.

debrief.saw: A close just above the high, then a close back below and a move away.
debrief.know: Price traded above the prior high and failed to sustain: sweep-like behavior.
debrief.unknown: Whether this becomes a reversal. That’s a structure question for later.

items.text: Price traded above the prior high.
Buy-side liquidity above the high may have been taken.
items.why: Reasonable: price traded where buy-side may rest. Note the “may.”
Nothing closed through the HL. Structure hasn’t changed.
That’s a prediction, not an observation.

items.text: Big players trapped the breakout buyers.
items.why: The chart can’t show who traded or why.

levels.prompt: What do we know, and what don’t we know yet?
levels.name: Structure or liquidity?

debrief.saw: A wick above the prior high and a close back below, with the HL intact.
debrief.know: Price traded above, closed back below, and buy-side may have been taken.
debrief.unknown: Whether structure changes, where price goes, and who traded.

steps.text: Three traders describe the same two candles.

options.label: A: That was manipulation by the big banks
options.feedback: The chart can’t prove intent or identity.

options.label: B: Short now, the sweep is done
options.feedback: That turns context into an entry.

options.label: C: Price traded above the previous high and closed back below it

levels.name: Don’t overlabel it
levels.goal: Say what price did. Nothing more.

debrief.saw: A wick above the previous high and a close back below.
debrief.know: Price traded above the previous high and closed back below it.
debrief.unknown: Who traded, why, and what price does next.

steps.text: Price traded above the equal highs, then came back down.

options.label: Internal: the equal highs inside the range
options.why: Internal equal highs. The external high is untouched.

options.label: External: the range high
options.feedback: Look up. The external high is far above.

options.label: Both
options.feedback: Only one of them was traded through.

debrief.saw: Price traded above equal highs inside the range. The external high stayed far above.
debrief.know: Internal equal-high liquidity was taken. External liquidity was not.
debrief.unknown: Whether price will ever reach the external high.

steps.text: A beautiful sweep below the prior low, then a strong push up.

asks.prompt: DO YOU HAVE A DAYLI ICC ENTRY?

options.label: Yes, look at that sweep
options.feedback: Beautiful, yes. But a sweep isn’t part of the entry sequence.

options.label: No
options.why: Good read. A beautiful sweep is still context.

lens.context: Sweep-like behavior below the prior low.
lens.execution: Entry model: not present / not being evaluated yet

levels.name: The Dayli trap
levels.goal: Pretty isn’t the same as permission.

debrief.saw: A clean sweep below the prior low and a strong push higher.
debrief.know: Sell-side below the prior low was traded through and price recovered. Useful context.
debrief.unknown: Whether the Dayli ICC sequence ever forms here.
debrief.good: ✓ GOOD READ. You didn’t let a pretty sweep become an entry.

steps.text: Bullish structure. Price dipped below an internal low, closed back above, and is pushing up toward the HH.

options.label: Liquidity and structure provide useful bullish context, but a Dayli ICC entry cannot be assumed until the actual entry model forms.
options.why: That’s a disciplined read: context from two lenses, and execution kept separate.

options.label: Internal sell-side was swept in a bullish structure, so buy now.
options.feedback: That turns context into an entry.

options.label: Price will take the buy-side above the HH next.
Nothing useful here.
options.feedback: There’s plenty of useful context. It just isn’t an entry.

lens.context: Internal sell-side traded through and recovered. Buy-side may rest above the HH.
lens.execution: Entry model: not present / not being evaluated yet

levels.name: Final boss
levels.goal: Structure. Liquidity. Execution. Keep them separate.

debrief.saw: A bullish structure, a dip below an internal low that recovered, and price heading toward the HH.
debrief.know: Structure is bullish and the liquidity picture adds supportive context.
debrief.unknown: Whether the Dayli ICC entry sequence forms. Until it does, there’s no entry.

questionBank.question: Your friend says, “Liquidity is a secret trap the market sets for us.” What’s a better description?
options: Liquidity is about available orders: buyers and sellers willing to trade at a price
Liquidity is where price must go next
Liquidity is only the stops of retail traders
questionBank.why: Liquidity is about available orders. Not a trap, not a destination.

questionBank.question: Price is approaching an obvious previous high. What can you reasonably say?
options: Orders may be resting around it
There are exactly 5,000 stops above it
Price will definitely trade above it
Banks are waiting there to trap you
questionBank.why: An obvious level may attract orders. The chart can’t show counts, intent or the future.

questionBank.question: Where does buy-side liquidity commonly sit?
options: In the middle of a range
questionBank.why: Above highs: short stops and breakout buys are buy orders.

questionBank.question: A long trader’s stop below a swing low is part of…
questionBank.why: A long exits by selling, so that stop is a sell order below a low.

questionBank.question: Buy-side liquidity sits above the current high. What does that tell you about where price goes next?
options: Nothing guaranteed. It describes where orders may rest
Price must go up to take it
questionBank.why: It names orders, not a destination.

questionBank.question: Why do stops tend to cluster above obvious highs?
options: Many shorts read the same structure and pick similar logical spots
The market tells traders where to place them
Stops are always placed at round numbers
questionBank.why: Predictable structure can create predictable order placement.

questionBank.question: Price wicks below your stop, then rallies. What does the chart prove?
options: Price traded below the low before moving up
The market knows where your stop is
questionBank.why: The chart shows what price did, not intent.

questionBank.question: Which is the most likely liquidity pool area?
options: Just beyond equal highs at the top of a range
The open of a random candle
questionBank.why: Obvious highs, lows, equal highs/lows, range and session extremes.

questionBank.question: You spot equal highs. What can you conclude?
options: It’s an obvious area worth monitoring
The trend is about to reverse

questionBank.question: Inside a defined range, price trades above an internal high. The external high is far above. Which liquidity was taken?
questionBank.why: Price is still inside the room.

questionBank.question: What do you need before you can call liquidity internal or external?
questionBank.why: Define the range first. Then ask: which liquidity?

questionBank.question: Previous high: 20,000. Price trades to 20,008, then closes at 19,992. The most objective description?
options: Price traded above the previous high and failed to sustain above it
questionBank.why: Observation first. Then you can call it sweep-like behavior.

questionBank.question: Price sweeps a high. What does that prove?
options: That price traded through an area where orders may rest

questionBank.question: Bearish structure. Price wicks above a minor internal high and closes back below. The relevant lower high is untouched. Your friend says it’s an MSS. What’s missing?
options: A close through the relevant lower high
questionBank.why: MSS is a structure event: a close through the relevant swing.

questionBank.question: Price closes above the prior high, holds above it and builds a higher low. Best description?
Is a liquidity sweep a required Dayli ICC entry condition?
options: No. Liquidity is context, not a required condition
questionBank.why: Learn more so you can understand more. Not so you can require more.
